recognize_zh: 兩顆相鄰的卵圓形細胞，整個細胞質被密集的深紫黑色顆粒填滿，顆粒還溢出到細胞邊緣外，中央隱約可見單一圓核，這種單核、顆粒濃密到遮蓋核的外觀就是骨髓中的肥大細胞（mast cell）。
features: Two adjacent oval cells, larger than nearby lymphocytes
Single round-to-oval centrally placed nucleus, partially obscured by granules
Cytoplasm packed with dense, uniform, deep purple-black metachromatic granules
Granules extend to and slightly beyond the cell border, giving a fuzzy outline
Round/oval (not spindled) cell shape without hypogranularity or bilobed nuclei
Background of fibrillar stromal strands, red cells and small lymphoid cells
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows two oval cells with a single central round nucleus and cytoplasm densely packed with coarse, deep purple-black granules that partially obscure the nucleus and extend to the cell margin. The cells are round to oval rather than spindle-shaped, and there is no hypogranularity, nuclear lobation or clustering to suggest atypia. Surrounding stroma and scattered lymphoid cells are present. Findings are consistent with normal (typical) tissue mast cells in the bone marrow.

ddx.vs: Basophils are smaller with a segmented/lobulated nucleus and fewer, larger water-soluble granules, whereas mast cells are mononuclear with densely packed smaller granules.

ddx.dx: Neoplastic mast cells in systemic mastocytosis
ddx.vs: Neoplastic mast cells are often spindle-shaped, hypogranular, with eccentric or bilobed nuclei and form aggregates, expressing CD25/CD2 and KIT D816V.
Siderophages have irregular coarse blue-black pigment of variable size, a more abundant cytoplasm and are Prussian blue positive.
Promyelocytes have finer azurophilic granules, a paranuclear hof and less dense granulation that does not obscure the nucleus.
